proposedTopics.title: Two Pointers
proposedTopics.description: Two indices scanning data (often after sorting) to avoid nested loops. Builds directly on array/hash foundations.

proposedTopics.title: Opposite-direction pointers
proposedTopics.description: One pointer at each end of a sorted structure, moving inward based on a comparison. Recognize: sorted array, "pair/triplet meeting a condition", area/capacity maximization.

proposedTopics.title: Fast & slow pointers (array)
proposedTopics.description: A slow write-pointer trails a fast read-pointer to compact/filter an array in place. Recognize: "remove duplicates in place", "move zeroes", in-place filtering with O(1) space.

proposedTopics.title: Three-way partitioning
proposedTopics.description: Dutch national flag: low/mid/high pointers partition into three buckets in one pass. Recognize: "sort with only 3 distinct values", partition-around-pivot.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for converging (opposite-direction) two pointers? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: sorted (or sortable) array, "pair/triplet meeting a condition", maximize area/capacity between two ends. Move the pointer that can only improve the objective. Pitfall: sorting when the problem wants original indices, or failing to skip duplicate values on the inner scan (double-counts triplets). Related: Valid Palindrome converges from both ends on characters.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the converging two-pointer loop in your language of choice: given a sorted array and a target, return whether some pair sums to the target.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: lo=0, hi=n-1; while lo<hi compare sum to target: too small -> lo++, too big -> hi--, equal -> found. Invariant: every pair with one index outside [lo,hi] has already been ruled out.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted (Medium) — return the 1-based indices of the two numbers that add up to target.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Converge from both ends: move lo up when the sum is too small, hi down when too big — no hash map needed since it is sorted.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Container With Most Water (Medium) — pick two lines forming the container that holds the most water.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Width shrinks as you move inward, so always advance the shorter wall — moving the taller one can never increase area.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: 3Sum (Medium) — return all unique triplets that sum to zero.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Sort, then for each i run a converging two-pointer scan on the rest; skip equal values at every level to avoid duplicate triplets.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Trapping Rain Water (Hard) — compute how much water is trapped between the bars after raining.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Two pointers tracking leftMax and rightMax; water above a bar is bounded by the smaller side, so advance from whichever side has the lower running max.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for the slow-write / fast-read two-pointer compaction? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "remove/filter in place", "move X to the end", O(1) extra space over an array you may reorder. Slow marks the next write slot; fast scans. Pitfall: incrementing slow when you skip an element (only advance it after a write), or clobbering unread data. Related: Remove Element uses the same write-pointer idea.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the in-place compaction loop in your language of choice: given an array and a keep-predicate, move all kept elements to the front and return the new length.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: slow=0; for fast over the array, if keep(arr[fast]) then arr[slow]=arr[fast]; slow++. Invariant: arr[0..slow) is exactly the kept elements seen so far, in order.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array (Easy) — remove duplicates in place so each value appears once, return the new length.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Slow write-pointer; write arr[fast] only when it differs from the last kept value (arr[slow-1]).

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Move Zeroes (Easy) — move all zeroes to the end in place while keeping the order of non-zero elements.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Write pointer collects non-zeros to the front; fill the remainder with zeroes (or swap as you go).

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for Dutch-national-flag three-way partitioning? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "sort with only 3 distinct values/categories", partition around a pivot into <, ==, > in one pass with O(1) space. Pitfall: advancing mid after swapping with high — the value pulled from high is unexamined, so re-check it before moving on. Related: Kth Largest Element in an Array uses the same partition step in quickselect (carded under Heap / Priority Queue).

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the Dutch-national-flag partition in your language of choice: given an array of values 0/1/2, sort it in a single pass with O(1) extra space.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: low, mid=0, high=n-1; while mid<=high: 0 -> swap(low,mid), low++, mid++; 1 -> mid++; 2 -> swap(mid,high), high-- (do NOT advance mid). Invariant: [0,low) are 0s, [low,mid) are 1s, (high,n) are 2s.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Sort Colors (Medium) — sort an array of 0s, 1s, and 2s in place in one pass.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Three pointers (low/mid/high): swap 0s to the front, 2s to the back, leave 1s in the middle; don't advance mid after a swap with high.
